- scripts/unblock_judge.sh: 166-173 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: remove_label ignores HTTP 404 (label already absent) but the error string match `grep -q 'HTTP 404'` only matches when gh api stderr contains that exact substring. If gh's error format changes (e.g., to "404 Not Found" without "HTTP" prefix), the guard will fail closed and block the resume command, which would be a regression from the prior behavior that always failed on any DELETE error.
  WHY: The human-written curl/gh stderr for a 404 label deletion could vary across gh versions or proxy layers. If the stderr message format changes, the grep will miss, ops_failed will be set, and the resume command will be blocked even though the label was genuinely absent.

After the 6-hour cooldown, the scan re-dispatches the judge, the ledger returns a terminal close verdict, and the telegram block at line 291-292 fires again with the same pending-closure message. Operators receive duplicate CRITICAL alerts for what is essentially one unresolved failure.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh: 168-173 (remove_label branch, modified in LAST RUN DIFF) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The new 404-handling is correct for the race it targets, but the check `if ! grep -q 'HTTP 404' "${RUNTIME_DIR}/remove_label_error.txt"` only matches the literal substring "HTTP 404". `gh api` writes the message to stderr as "gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)" on failure paths but other operations can emit "HTTP 404" substrings (for example a 404 on a related endpoint that succeeded at the DELETE level). The check is too permissive: any stderr line containing "HTTP 404" suppresses the failure flag, even when the actual operation returned a different status.
  WHY: If a previous `gh api` call in the same job left a stale "HTTP 404" in a different file that shares the variable, or if the API's stderr ever includes an unexpected "HTTP 404" while the DELETE itself returned 5xx, the suppress could wrongly accept the failure. The current code is safe enough because `RUNTIME_DIR` is per-run and the variable is overwritten on each call, but the failure-message matching itself is broader than the documented contract of "gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)".
- Requirement: The root `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` carries the legacy in-session wording while `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` has the updated Claude-engine orchestrator hand-off wording. `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:30` (test_template_parity) reads both files and asserts byte equality — this test is currently failing in `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, which in turn makes the aggregate `lint` job red.
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/audit-plans.md
  Evidence of absence: PR #6243 and earlier rounds have repeatedly been unable to update the root command because the review editor's transfer allowlist (`scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:34`) excludes `.claude/commands/**`, so the autofix keeps reporting the gap as a deferred issue. The CI failure is real, active, and the parity test will fail again on the next push until either the root command is updated to match the template or the parity test is weakened.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py: line 40 (the `allowed()` allowlist tuple)
  PROBLEM: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` is referenced in `agents.md:234` and `.claude/settings.json:92,112` as a tracked runtime hook, but the `allowed()` function's allowlist only permits `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` and `.github/ai/claude_engine.json` for the `.claude/` prefix. Future rounds that try to fix a parity drift in the root merge-status guard (the pattern that caused multiple earlier autofix failures) will hit the same "excluded from transfer" blocker.
  WHY: Add `".claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py"` to the allowlist tuple at line 40 so the autofix can deliver root hook parity fixes that the byte-identity contract demands.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
